spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The decisive move is to stop forcing one Dirichlet polynomial to satisfy incompatible length and moment demands. A polynomial of length T^(1/W) only admits useful control for O(W) moments, while shortening it worsens the log-zeta majorant; moreover, Markov bounds from moments do not reconstruct sharp large-value frequencies. Splitting the polynomial into blocks lets later, longer, lower-variance pieces be raised to smaller powers, and working directly with truncated exponential moments avoids the lossy tail-reconstruction step.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source identifies two losses in the earlier route: usable moments decrease as Dirichlet-polynomial length increases, and Markov-inequality tail estimates are not optimal even given moment information. It proposes A=sum_j A_j, bounds |zeta|^(2k) by the product of exp(2k Re A_j), truncates each exponential when its block is controlled, and handles a point with an oversized block using a shorter log-zeta majorant together with the small measure of such points.
directed.conceptual_reading: This is a multiscale compatibility repair. The block decomposition allocates different proof budgets to components according to their expected contribution and admissible moment order; exceptional points are localized by the first failed scale rather than making the whole approximation uniformly short. Direct exponential-moment control also preserves the quantity ultimately needed instead of passing through an insufficient tail summary.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is from the additive representation A=sum_j A_j to the multiplicative representation exp(2k Re A)=product_j exp(2k Re A_j). Expected block-size control makes each factor replaceable by a short polynomial, while an oversized block becomes an exceptional-set witness that licenses changing to a shorter cutoff.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This span gives the proof architecture, not the estimates that justify the truncations, exceptional-set measures, or product integrals. It produces an upper-bound mechanism only and does not establish a sharp large-value distribution or a Gaussian limit.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The expanded positive truncations are kept short enough that time integration becomes a prime-multiplicity test. The geometric block scales and block-dependent degrees force the total prime product below a small power of T, allowing Proposition 2 to replace the cosine integral by T times a nonnegative square-supported function f plus a negligible error. Multiplicativity then reassembles the many indices into independent block factors.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: After expanding both squares and every block polynomial, the product of all participating primes is bounded by T^0.1 using the geometric beta_i progression, the truncation degrees, and the small terminal beta_I. Proposition 2 evaluates each cosine-product integral as T f(product)+O(T^0.1). Since f is nonnegative, the original weighted coefficients C are dominated by reciprocal-square-root coefficients D. The accumulated error is bounded by T^0.2 (log log T)^(2k), and multiplicativity of f converts the main sum into a product over blocks, recovering coefficients with powers of 2k.
directed.conceptual_reading: This is the deterministic realization of an independence heuristic. Short total Dirichlet length makes oscillatory time integration act like an orthogonality filter; f records exactly the surviving even-multiplicity configurations. Disjoint prime blocks and multiplicativity then expose a product structure analogous to independent increments without assuming probabilistic independence.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The proof passes from an analytic integral of products of cosines to a combinatorial sum indexed by prime tuples, with f as the bridge object encoding square support. It then uses coefficient domination and multiplicativity to compress that tuple sum back into blockwise products. The domination forgets some smooth weights in exchange for a tractable upper bound.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The step depends on Proposition 2 and on the verified short-length inequality. Replacing C by D and estimating the error are one-sided losses. This unit stops before evaluating the square-supported multiplicities; that collapse occurs in the next unit.
directed.uncertainty: The qualitative reduction and the T^0.1/T^0.2 bounds are clear, but the dense extracted products and multi-indices carry high formula-layout risk; exact reuse should retain the checked span or scan.
